column1: #mapping_set_title: CALM to MITRE ATT&CK class mappings

#mapping_set_description: "Schema-level mappings between the FINOS Common Architecture Language Model (CALM 1.2) and the MITRE ATT&CK LinkML schema. CALM's architecture primitives serve as threat modelling anchors: Node maps to ATT&CK Asset (things adversaries target); Control maps to ATT&CK Mitigation (defences applied to nodes); Relationship maps to ATT&CK AttackRelationship. These mappings support CALM-based threat modelling by anchoring CALM elements into the ATT&CK knowledge base."

column7: A CALM Node is a logical or physical architecture element (system, service, database, network); an ATT&CK Asset is an infrastructure component that adversaries may target - when a CALM Node is an IT infrastructure element it aligns directly with the ATT&CK Asset concept.

A CALM Control is a domain-scoped security control applied to an architecture element; an ATT&CK Mitigation describes a security measure that limits the impact or likelihood of an adversary technique - both represent applied defences to system components.

A CALM Relationship is a typed directed link between nodes; an ATT&CK AttackRelationship expresses how ATT&CK objects (groups, techniques, mitigations, assets) relate - related as both are structured typed edges in their respective directed graphs.

A CALM Flow captures the sequential traversal of a business process over architecture nodes; an ATT&CK Tactic represents a high-level adversary goal category (e.g. Initial Access, Lateral Movement) - related as both describe high-level ordered activity sequences across system elements.

A CALM ControlRequirement specifies the domain definition of a control; an ATT&CK Technique describes a specific adversary method that a control must defend against - related in that control requirements are often derived from or validated against known attack techniques.
